turns.assessment: The simultaneous two errored seconds across many channels, accompanied by protection switching at t=600 and restoration 1.6 s later, indicates a brief common optical impairment rather than a client, OTN-switch, or individual-channel failure. The absence of changes in received power, OSNR, BER trends, DGD, amplifier telemetry, and channel monitors strongly favors a millisecond-scale SOP transient on the common optical path toward S03. The evidence does not identify which upstream fibre span was disturbed, so no element-specific repair can be committed safely.

proposals.rationale: Multiple line interfaces and services accumulated exactly two errored seconds at the same time, while protected services switched briefly and returned. A fast polarization transient can cause this without a persistent alarm or observable change in sampled optical power, OSNR, DGD, or amplifier telemetry. The affected receivers at and downstream of S03 point to a shared upstream fibre route, but the individual span cannot be distinguished.
A brief physical disturbance could produce the synchronized transient, but its expected power excursion should be more likely to appear in the extensive power monitoring; none did.
